560:
In all areas of special flood hazard, the following provisions are required:
(1) New construction and/or substantial improvements.
a. Where base flood elevation data are available, new construction and/or substantial improvement of any structure or manufactured home shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated no lower than one foot above the base flood elevation. Should solid foundation perimeter walls be used to elevate a structure, openings sufficient to facilitate equalization of flood hydrostatic forces on both sides of exterior walls shall be provided in accordance with standards of section 16-285(4).
b. All heating and air conditioning equipment and components (including ductwork), all electrical, ventilation, plumbing, and other service facilities shall be elevated at or above one foot above the base flood elevation.
(2) Nonresidential construction. New construction and/or the substantial improvement of any structure located in A1-30, AE, or AH zones may be floodproofed in lieu of elevation. The structure, together with attendant utility and sanitary facilities, must be designed to be watertight to one foot above the base flood elevation, with walls substantially impermeable to the passage of water and structural components having the capability of resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads and the effect of buoyancy. A registered professional engineer or architect shall certify that the design and methods of construction are in accordance with accepted standards of practice for meeting the provisions above, and shall provide such certification to the official as set forth above and in section 16-253(6).
(3) Manufactured homes and recreational vehicles. Where base flood elevation data are available:
a. All manufactured homes placed and/or substantially improved:
1. On individual lots or parcels;
2. In new and/or substantially improved manufactured home parks or subdivisions;
3. In expansions to existing manufactured home parks or subdivisions; or
4. On a site in an existing manufactured home park or subdivision where a manufactured home has incurred "substantial damage" as the result of a flood;
must have the lowest floor including basement, elevated no lower than one foot above the base flood elevation.
b. Manufactured homes placed and/or substantially improved in an existing manufactured home park or subdivision may be elevated so that either:
1. The lowest floor of the manufactured home is elevated no lower than one foot above the level of the base flood elevation; or
2. The manufactured home chassis is elevated and supported by reinforced piers (or other foundation elements of at least an equivalent strength) no less than 36 inches in height above grade.
c. All manufactured homes must be securely anchored to an adequately anchored foundation system to resist flotation, collapse and lateral movement as set forth in section 16-285(6).
d. All recreational vehicles placed on sites must:
1. Be on the site for fewer than 180 consecutive days;
2. Be fully licensed and ready for highway use, (a recreational vehicle is ready for highway use if it is licensed, on its wheels or jacking system, attached to the site only by quick disconnect type utilities and security devices, and has no permanently attached structures or additions); or
3. Meet all the requirements of new construction, including the anchoring and elevation requirements of section 16-286(3).
(4) Floodway. Located within areas of special flood hazard established in section 16-185 are areas designated as floodways. A floodway may be an extremely hazardous area due to velocity floodwaters, debris or erosion potential. In addition, the area must remain free of encroachment in order to allow for the discharge of the base flood without increased flood heights. Therefore, the following provisions shall apply:
a. Encroachments are prohibited, including earthen fill, new construction, substantial improvements or other development within the regulatory floodway. Development may be permitted, however, provided that it is demonstrated through hydrologic and hydraulic analyses performed in accordance with standard engineering practice that the encroachment shall not result in any increase in flood levels or floodway widths during a base flood discharge. A registered professional engineer must provide supporting technical data and certification thereof.
b. If subsection 4(a) of this section is satisfied, then any new construction or substantial improvement shall comply with all other applicable flood hazard reduction provisions of this division 4.
(Ord. of 10-12-2010, art. 4, § B)
561:
Located within the areas of special flood hazard established in section 16-185, where streams exist but no base flood data have been provided (A-zones), or where base flood data have been provided but a floodway has not been delineated, the following provisions apply:
(1) When base flood elevation data or floodway data have not been provided in accordance with section 16-185, then the mayor shall obtain, review, and reasonably utilize any scientific or historic base flood elevation and floodway data available from a federal, state, or other source in order to administer the provisions of division 4 of this article. Only if data are not available from these sources, then the following provisions shall apply:
a. No encroachments, including structures or fill material, shall be located within an area equal to the width of the stream or 20 feet, whichever is greater, measured from the top of the stream bank, unless certification by a registered professional engineer is provided demonstrating that such encroachment shall not result in more than a one foot increase in flood levels during the occurrence of the base flood discharge.
b. In special flood hazard areas without base flood elevation data, new construction and substantial improvements of existing structures shall have the lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area (including basement) elevated no less than three feet above the highest adjacent grade at the building site. The lowest floor is required to be elevated one foot above the estimated base flood elevation in A zone areas where a limited detail study has been completed. Openings sufficient to facilitate the unimpeded movements of floodwaters shall be provided in accordance with standards of section 16-285(4).
c. All heating and air conditioning equipment and components (including ductwork), all electrical, ventilation, plumbing, and other service facilities shall be elevated no less than three feet above the highest adjacent grade at the building site.
The mayor shall certify the lowest floor elevation level and the record shall become a permanent part of the permit file.
(Ord. of 10-12-2010, art. 4, § C)
562:
Located within the areas of special flood hazard established in section 16-185, where streams with base flood elevations are provided but no floodways have been designated (AE zones), the following provisions apply:
(1) No encroachments, including fill material, new structures or substantial improvements shall be located within areas of special flood hazard, unless certification by a registered professional engineer is provided demonstrating that the cumulative effect of the proposed development, when combined with all other existing and anticipated development, will not increase the water surface elevation of the base flood more than one foot at any point within the community. The engineering certification should be supported by technical data that conforms to standard hydraulic engineering principles.
(2) New construction or substantial improvements of buildings shall be elevated or flood-proofed to elevations established in accordance with section 16-286.
(Ord. of 10-12-2010, art. 4, § D)
563:
Areas of special flood hazard established in section 16-185 may include designated shallow flooding areas (AO zones). These areas have base flood depths of one to three feet above ground, with no clearly defined channel. The following provisions apply:
(1) All new construction and substantial improvements of residential and non-residential structures shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated to the flood depth number specified on the flood insurance rate map (FIRM), above the highest adjacent grade. If no flood depth number is specified, the lowest floor, including basement, shall be elevated at least three feet above the highest adjacent grade. A registered professional engineer or architect shall certify that the design and methods of construction are in accordance with accepted standards of practice for meeting the provisions above, and shall provide such certification to the official as required in section 16-252.
(4) Drainage paths shall be provided to guide floodwater around and away from any proposed structure.
(Ord. of 10-12-2010, art. 4, § E)
564:
(a) All subdivision and/or development proposals shall be consistent with the need to minimize flood damage.
(b) All subdivision and/or development proposals shall have public utilities and facilities such as sewer, gas, electrical and water systems located and constructed to minimize flood damage.
(c) All subdivision and/or development proposals shall have adequate drainage provided to reduce exposure to flood hazards.

(Ord. of 10-12-2010, art. 4, § F)
565:
(a) Critical facilities shall not be located in the 100-year floodplain or the 500-year floodplain.

(Ord. of 10-12-2010, art. 4, § G)
568:
(a) The planning and zoning board as established by the City of Reidsville shall hear and decide requests for appeals or variance from the requirements of this article.
(b) The planning and zoning board shall hear and decide appeals when it is alleged an error in any requirement, decision, or determination is made by the city building inspector in the enforcement or administration of this article.
(c) Any person aggrieved by the decision of the planning and zoning board may appeal such decision to the Superior Court of Tattnall County, as provided in O.C.G.A. § 5-4-1.
(d) Variances may be issued for the repair or rehabilitation of historic structures upon a determination that the proposed repair or rehabilitation will not preclude the structure's continued designation as a historic structure and the variance is the minimum to preserve the historic character and design of the structure.
(e) Variances may be issued for development necessary for the conduct of a functionally dependent use, provided that the criteria of this article are met, no reasonable alternative exists, and the development is protected by methods that minimize flood damage during the base flood and create no additional threats to public safety.
(f) Variances shall not be issued within any designated floodway if any increase in flood levels during the base flood discharge would result.
(g) In reviewing such requests, the planning and zoning board shall consider all technical evaluations, relevant factors, and all standards specified in this and other sections of this article.
(h) Conditions for variances.
(1) A variance shall be issued only when there is:
a. A finding of good and sufficient cause;
b. A determination that failure to grant the variance would result in exceptional hardship; and
c. A determination that the granting of a variance will not result in increased flood heights, additional threats to public safety, extraordinary public expense, create nuisance, cause fraud on or victimization of the public, or conflict with existing local laws or ordinances.
(2) The provisions of this article are minimum standards for flood loss reduction; therefore any deviation from the standards must be weighed carefully. Variances shall only be issued upon a determination that the variance is the minimum necessary, considering the flood hazard, to afford relief; and, in the instance of a historic structure, a determination that the variance is the minimum necessary so as not to destroy the historic character and design of the building.
(3) Any applicant to whom a variance is granted shall be given written notice specifying the difference between the base flood elevation and the elevation of the proposed lowest floor and stating that the cost of flood insurance will be commensurate with the increased risk to life and property resulting from the reduced lowest floor elevation.
(4) The zoning board shall maintain the records of all appeal actions and report any variances to the Federal Emergency Management Agency upon request.
Upon consideration of the factors listed above and the purposes of this ordinance, the city planning and zoning board may attach such conditions to the granting of variances as it deems necessary to further the purposes of this article.
(Ord. of 10-12-2010, art. 5)

572:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Hazardous waste or material means any waste or material which, because of its quantity, concentration or physical, chemical or infectious characteristics, may:

573:
There is hereby established a use district to be known as a wellhead protection zone, identified and described as all the area within a circle the center of which is the center of any city water supply wellhead and the radius of which is 250 feet.
(Ord. of 1-10-1994, § 3)
574:
The following uses shall be permitted within wellhead protection zones:
(1) Any use permitted within existing agricultural or single-family residential lot size for a lot any portion of which lies within the wellhead protection zone shall not be less one acre; and
(2) Any other open land use where any building located on the property is incidental and accessory to the primary open land use.
(Ord. of 1-10-1994, § 4)
576:
The policies and procedures for administration of any wellhead protection zone established under this article, including without limitation those applicable to nonconforming uses, exceptions, enforcement and penalties, shall be the same as provided in the existing zoning ordinance for the city, as the same is presently enacted or may from time to time be amended.
(Ord. of 1-10-1994, § 6)

The fire department shall be headed by a fire chief and shall be composed of such other paid and volunteer members and employees as may be determined necessary by the city council.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-1)
583:
Whenever the fire department is answering an alarm or operating at the scene of a fire or other emergency, every enrolled member of the department is hereby empowered and authorized to control and direct motor vehicle traffic, stop or move vehicles, and enforce all provisions of this article and any other code provisions, the enforcement of which are deemed necessary to assist in the control of the fire or other emergency.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-3)
584:
No person other than a duly enrolled member of the fire department shall ride upon the fire trucks of the city at any time, or use, borrow or interfere with any fire department equipment, or attempt to use the equipment at the scene of a fire unless authorized to do so by the fire chief.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-2)
588:
(a) The provisions of this article shall apply to all buildings, structures, premises, facilities, and applicable conditions within the city. They shall apply to existing as well as new buildings, structures, premises, facilities, and applicable conditions and whenever a covered activity creates a distinct hazard from fire or its associated hazards to life or to the property of another.
(b) The provisions of this article shall apply in addition to and in supplementation of the provisions of the fire code adopted by reference in section 8-52 (International Fire Code, 2006 Edition). In the event of conflict, the provisions of this article shall control.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(a))
591:
The implementation of these provisions shall be administered by the fire chief, and may be applied or enforced as he deems appropriate and necessary to gain reasonable, realistic, and practical minimum compliance with the purpose and intent of this article within the city. The fire chief is authorized to seek compliance with applicable state fire and life safety standards within the city in accordance with state law, procedures, rules, regulations and orders.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(b))
592:
The chief of police, the city building inspector, or law enforcement officers of the city shall render assistance to the fire chief in the implementation and enforcement of this Code upon the request of the fire chief.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(c))
593:
(a) The fire chief or his authorized representatives may, to the extent permitted by law, have free access to and the right to enter at all reasonable times any building, structure, facility or premises coming under the scope of this code, whether completed or under construction, for the purpose of conducting inspections and otherwise implementing the provisions of this article.
(b) Before entering any building, structure, facility or premises not normally open to the public, except when a fire or other emergency condition exists or has occurred, the fire chief or his representatives shall obtain the consent of the occupant, owner, or person in charge at the time. Where consent to enter is refused, the fire chief may seek an order or administrative search warrant from the municipal court of the city, or if deemed appropriate, from the superior court of the county authorizing his entry or that of his representatives for the purpose of conducting the inspection or investigation.
(c) The term "emergency condition," for purposes of this section, means any condition or circumstance which the fire chief judges to constitute an immediate threat or danger to the occupants of the building, structure, facility or premises or the public or exposed property from fire, explosion or threat of fire or explosion.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(d))
594:
Any application for or the acceptance of any approval, permit, license or certificate requested, or required pursuant to this code or applicable law or ordinance of this city or state, constitutes agreement and consent by the person, firm or corporation making the application, or accepting the approval, permit, license or certificate to allow the fire chief or his designees to enter the building, structure or premises at any reasonable time to conduct inspections as may be deemed appropriate by the fire chief or as otherwise provided by this article or other applicable ordinances, regulations or state law.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(e))
595:
(a) The fire chief is authorized to inspect or cause to be inspected, as resources permit, buildings, structures, premises and facilities coming within the scope of this code, as he deems appropriate or necessary based on fire experience in the community, on complaint, or other applicable grounds, for the purposes of ascertaining if any conditions exist which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire or explosion, or that could contribute to the spread of a fire or its byproducts, or any significant nonconformance with the purposes or provisions of this article or of any other law, rule or regulation affecting safety to the life or property from fire, explosion, or the hazards related to same.
(b) The fire chief is authorized to apply other applicable laws, and to cause to be corrected any conditions which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire or explosion, or that could contribute to the spread of a fire, or any significant nonconformance with the purposes or provisions of this code affecting safety to life or property from fire, explosion or to the hazards related to same.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(f))
596:
(a) Whenever the fire chief or his designated representatives find any significant violations of this code or any significant fire hazards as defined this code, he is authorized to issue or serve a written notice of the findings of an inspection as set forth in this section.
(b) Whenever the fire chief or his designated representatives find any violations of this code or any fire hazards that are deemed to create a serious potential for fire or explosion or which is deemed to create a serious potential threat to life in the event of fire or explosion, he is authorized to issue a written order to correct or abate the violations or hazards. Such order, when issued, shall set forth a reasonable and realistic time or date limit for correction, abatement or compliance. The time for correction, abatement and compliance established by or as directed by the fire chief may be reasonably correlated by him to the seriousness or relative degree of hazard, as determined by him, and or to the complexity of the means of correction or abatement.
(c) Where deemed necessary by the fire chief, he may issue a verbal order for immediate correction or abatement followed by a written order or notice of action.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(g))
597:
(a) The service of notices or orders issued pursuant to this article may be made by the fire chief or his representatives upon the owner, occupant or person in charge of the building, structure, facility, premises or portion thereof where the hazards or violations were found, or by delivering a copy of the notice or order to any or all of the persons noted.
(b) In the event such person or persons cannot be served by delivery as noted, service may be accomplished by affixing a copy of the notice or order in a conspicuous place at or near the entrance of the building, structure, facility or premises, or by delivering or sending a copy of the notice or order to the known agent of the owner or occupant, or in the event of an absentee owner with no known agent, by sending a copy by certified or registered mail to the owner's last known residence, business or post office address.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(h))
598:
(a) Any person who shall fail to comply with an order or correction of abatement issued pursuant to this article, or who shall build or act in violation of this Code or of any detailed statement of specifications or plans submitted and approved under authority of this Code in connection with any approval, certificate or permit issued thereunder, or who shall perform any act deemed to create a serious potential for fire or explosion and for which the issuance of an order to correct or abate is not adequate, and who is found guilty shall be guilty of a violation of this Code.
(b) For each violation and noncompliance, the violator shall be subject to penalties as provided in section 1-14. The imposition of penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation or permit it to continue, and the responsible persons shall be required to correct or abate such violations within a time limit as ordered by the court. When not otherwise specified, each five days that a prohibited condition or violation continues following an order of the court to correct or abate same shall constitute a separate offense.
(c) When the fire chief or his authorized representative determines that violations of this article warrant the filing of charges or action of the court, the issuing of a citation of charges or summons to appear before the municipal court of the city shall be served by any certified law enforcement officer to the city upon request of the fire chief or his authorized representative.
(d) In addition to the filing of charges as authorized by this section, or as a separate remedy at law, the fire chief may seek injunctive relief for any fire hazard, violation, or condition that threatens the safety of life based on the provisions of this article or any applicable ordinance of the city or state law.
(e) The application of penalties by the court as provided in this section shall not be held to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or violations.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(i))
599:
(a) It is unlawful for any person to remove any notice or order issued in connection with this code and affixed to a building, structure, facility or premises without the approval of the fire chief or his authorized representative.
(b) It is unlawful for any persons firm or corporation to use a building, structure, facility or premises in violation of the provisions of this article where an order has been affixed to same prohibiting the use of same under the authority of any provision of this article without the approval of the fire chief or his authorized representative or the court.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(j))
600:
The fire chief shall have the authority to summarily abate any violation of this code or any fire hazard as defined by this article which constitutes an immediate or imminent danger or threat to life in his opinion, and where following the provisions for abating corrective action or abatement as set forth elsewhere in this article is not practical in his judgment.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(k))
601:
(a) The fire chief shall have the authority to modify or waive any of the provisions of this article, or of the ordinances or standards adopted by reference as supplements to the provisions of this article, upon application in writing by the owners or occupants of a buildings, structure, facility or premises, or by his designated authorized agents, when there are practical difficulties in the way of carrying out the strict letter of this code or the codes or standards adopted by reference as supplements to the provisions of this article.
(b) Such modification or waiver may be granted by the fire chief, provided that in his judgment the spirit, intents and purposes of this article are observed, the public safety shall be reasonably and practically secured, the waiver or modification is in the interest of the community and substantial justice will be done. The particulars of any waiver or modification granted or allowed, and the decision of the fire chief thereon, shall be entered upon the records of the fire department.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(l))
602:
It is unlawful for any person to interfere with, abuse, or obstruct in any way the fire chief, or his representatives in carrying out any actions in accordance with their official duties as set forth by this article or by any other applicable local ordinances, or by state law or regulation.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(m))
603:
(a) The fire chief or his authorized representatives are authorized to investigate the cause, origin and circumstances of any fire or explosion, or to investigate any incident resulting from a false alarm or fire or a bomb threat.
(b) When, in the judgment of the fire chief, reasonable cause exists that a fire or explosion may have been of criminal origin, the fire chief or his authorized representatives are authorized to locate and take custody of any or all physical evidence relating to the cause of the fire or explosion and to continue the investigation to the extent deemed appropriate within the limits of fire department resources and within the limits of applicable state law.
(c) The fire chief shall inform the police department of each fire of criminal or suspected criminal origin and he shall assist the police department in its investigation if so requested by that department. The police department shall be responsible for the investigation of fires, explosions, false alarms or bomb threats of criminal origin or suspected criminal origin so as to identify, apprehend and assist in the prosecution of the persons responsible for the criminal acts.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(n))
604:
(a) Any officer or employee of the city empowered or authorized to administer or act under the provisions of this article, and acting for the city in the discharge of his duties, shall not be held liable personally, and he is hereby relieved from all personal liability from any damages that may accrue to any persons or property as a result of any act required, implied or permitted in the discharge of his duties, or as required, implied or permitted by this article, or as a result of the omission of any action required or authorized by this article. Any suit instituted against any officer or employee in connection with the implementation of the provisions of this article or in connection with any omission to carry out the provisions of this article shall be defended by the legal representative of the city until the matter is settled.
(b) The city shall not be liable for any damage to persons or property resulting from any act or any failure to act in connection with any provision of this article.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(o))
605:
When, in the judgment of the fire chief, or his authorized representatives in his absence, there is an actual or serious potential danger to the occupants or persons in close proximity of any building, structure, facility or premises because of an unsafe structural condition, the presence of explosives, explosive fumes or vapor, toxic fumes, gases or materials, the fire chief, or his authorized representatives in his absence, may order the complete or partial immediate evacuation of the building, structure, facility or premises and, as necessary, areas in such proximity to these as to be endangered. All persons under order to evacuate shall promptly leave the evacuation area and shall not reenter until authorized to do so by the official that issued the evacuation order.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-7(q))
606:
No person shall knowingly maintain a fire hazard, fire nuisance or a public nuisance as defined by this article and to knowingly maintain such is unlawful.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(a))
607:
No person shall knowingly permit or allow any fire to spread so as to endanger the life or property of another or use or operate any device or appliance which may be a source of ignition in any way so as to endanger life or property. No such device or appliance shall be used unless proper removal of combustible or flammable material surrounding the operation is accomplished or such other reasonable precautions are taken to ensure against the starting and spreading of fire.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(b))
608:
(a) No person shall kindle or maintain any bonfire or rubbish or any fire for the disposal of leaves, cut brush, etc., or authorize any such fire to be kindled or maintained on any public street or land. No such fire shall be kindled or maintained on any private land unless the location is not less that 50 feet of any building or structure, or the fire is contained in an approved waste burner located safely not less than 30 feet from any building or structure.
(b) Bonfires, rubbish fires or other outdoor fires shall be constantly attended by a competent and able-bodied person until such fire is extinguished. Such person shall have a garden hose connected to the water supply and readily available for use.
(c) The fire chief may prohibit or require the extinguishment of any or all bonfires, rubbish fires or other outdoor fires when atmospheric conditions or local circumstances make such fires a fire hazard or a fire nuisance.
(d) No person shall kindle or maintain any fire which produces offensive, noxious or toxic smoke, fumes, vapors or odors. Such fires and their byproducts are deemed to be a fire nuisance. Upon complaint of any person regarding smoke, fumes, vapors or odors from outdoor burning being conducted with or without a permit or other proper authorization, the person responsible for kindling or maintaining such fire shall promptly extinguish same or cause same to be extinguished upon verbal notice or order of the fire chief or his representative.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(c))
609:
No person shall kindle a fire upon the land of another without the permission of the owner thereof or his agent.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(d))
610:
No person shall deposit hot ashes, cinders, smoldering coals or substances subject to spontaneous ignition into any combustible receptacle, or place same within ten feet of any combustible materials; provided, however, the distance may be reduced to three feet if such materials are in a substantial metal container with a metal cover. Such container, unless resting on a noncombustible floor or on the ground outside the building, shall be placed in a noncombustible stand.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(e))
611:
(a) Whenever an unfriendly fire occurs in any building, structure or on any premises of any kind, the owner, manager, or any person discovering the fire, upon discovery of the fire or of evidence of there having been an unfriendly fire, even though it has apparently been extinguished, shall immediately cause notice of the existence of such fire, the circumstances of same and the location of same to be given to the city fire department.
(b) This requirement shall not be construed to forbid the owner, manager or other person in control of the aforementioned building or premises from using all reasonable diligence necessary to extinguish such fire while or after notification of it prior to the arrival of the fire department.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(f))
612:
It is unlawful for any person to make, issue, post or maintain any regulation, rule, order or policy, written or verbal, that would require any person to take any unnecessary delaying action prior to reporting a fire or related emergency or hazardous condition to the city fire department.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(g))
613:
Any person, upon discovering evidence of spontaneous heating or other abnormal heating of any merchandise, commodity, cargo, shipment or other material of any kind in any building, structure, appliance, apparatus, tank, vehicle, stack, pile or marine vessel, or any person discovering or being appraised of any uncontrolled leak or spill of a hazardous gas, liquid or other material, shall immediately notify the city police department.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(h))
614:
Any persons owning or having charge or control over any vacant building, including dwellings, shall remove all combustible waste, refuse, rubbish, or trash therefrom, and shall lock, barricade or otherwise secure all windows, doors and other openings in the building to prohibit entry by unauthorized persons. The premises shall be maintained clear of any waste, rubbish or hazardous material.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(i))
615:
(a) Use of torches or open flame for the removal of paint, or sweating pipe joints or for other purposes. Any person using a torch or other flame-producing device for removing paint from any building or structure or from any object within any building or structure, or for sweating pipe joints or for other purposes, shall be responsible for providing at least one approved fire extinguisher having at least a 2A classification or a water hose connected to a reliable water supply in the area where the open flame is being used.
(b) The person shall also be responsible for providing a fire watcher to remain at the building or structure to check for evidence of fire for at least one hour after the torch or flame-producing device has been used. When using any torch or other flame-producing device, combustible material in close proximity of the flame or device shall be protected against ignition by shielding, wetting or other reasonable and realistic means.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(j))
616:
It is unlawful to maintain any device utilizing an open flame at any excavation, road or any place where the dislodgment of such device might permit same to roll, fall or slide onto any forest or any land containing combustible material.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(k))
617:
(a) For the purposes of this article, a fire or emergency alarm shall be deemed and construed as being any act as follows: the giving, signaling, transmitting or communicating to any fire station, fire company, building occupants, or to any officer or employees thereof, whether by telephone, spoken word or other means of information or a signal to the effect that there is a fire or other emergency at or near the place indicated by the person giving, signaling, transmitting or communicating such information.
(b) It is unlawful for any person to give, signal, transmit or communicate or for any person to cause or permit or conspire with another to be given, signaled, transmitted or communicated in any manner any false fire or emergency alarm.
(c) It is unlawful for any person to tamper with or maliciously injure any fire or emergency alarm equipment, public or private, installed and maintained for the purpose of transmitting fire or emergency alarms for occupant notification or for transmitting fire or emergency alarms to the city fire department or other emergency service agency or organization that responds to emergency incidents in the city.
(d) Nothing in this article shall prohibit the sounding of any such signal essential for the carrying on of any fire or emergency drill.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(l))
618:
It is unlawful to transport or permit to be transported any asphalt or tar kettle beneath which is maintained any open fire, heated coals or ashes over any highway, road or street. Asphalt or tar kettles shall not be used inside of or on the roof of any building, or within ten feet of any building. Asphalt or tar kettles shall be in good working order and complete with an operation kettle lid. There shall be at least one approved portable fire extinguisher of a minimum 20B classification within 50 feet of each asphalt or tar kettle during the period such kettle is in use and one additional portable fire extinguisher of a least such classification on the roof being covered.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(m))
619:
(a) All new heating appliances, chimneys, incinerators, smokestacks, flues, or similar devices for producing heat, or for conveying smoke or hot gases to the outer air shall be installed, constructed, used and maintained in accordance with their listing, in accordance with the building code, mechanical code or gas code, or when not covered by such codes, with the applicable standards of this chapter and the fire code adopted in section 8-52.
(b) Existing installations may be continued in service subject to approval by the authority having jurisdiction. The fire chief may request the city gas and heating inspector, director of code enforcement or building official, as designated by the city council, to evaluate the installations to determine what additions or modifications must be made to reasonably ensure the installations meet a reasonable minimum level of safety so as not to create a fire hazard.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(n))
620:
Commercial cooking equipment for the new buildings, structures or occupancies shall be installed, protected and maintained in accordance with the fire code adopted by the city in section 8-52. Existing installations may be continued in service, subject to approval of the fire chief. If deemed necessary, the fire chief may require the installation of safety features deemed appropriate to reasonably ensure the cooking equipment meets a reasonable minimum level of safety so as not to create a fire hazard which endangers safety to life.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(o))
621:
Electrical wiring, equipment, fixtures and devices shall be installed, used and maintained in accordance with the electrical code or as appropriate the applicable standards of the fire code adopted by the city in section 8-52. Existing installations may be continued in service, subject to approval of the fire chief. If deemed necessary, the fire chief may request the city electrical inspector to inspect the installation to determine what additions or modifications must be made to reasonably ensure the installation meets a reasonable minimum level of safety so as not to create a fire hazard.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(p))
622:
Air conditioning and ventilating equipment, systems and related equipment newly installed shall be installed in accordance with the building code or mechanical code or when appropriate the applicable standards of the fire code adopted by the city in section 8-52. Existing installations may be continued in service, subject to approval by the fire chief if in his judgment a reasonable minimum level of safety is provided so as not to create a fire hazard.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(q))
623:
(a) Firewalls, fire stops and fire related partitions and floors required by this article, the building code or other applicable codes or laws shall be properly maintained. All openings made therein for the passages of pipes, electrical conduit, wiring and the like, and holes made for any reason shall be sealed with approved noncombustible material to protect against the passage of smoke or fire. Openings shall be protected in accordance with the applicable standards of the fire code adopted by the city in section 8-52.
(b) All the fire doors and smoke-stop doors shall be maintained in an operable condition. No fire door may be blocked, tied, obstructed or otherwise made inoperable. The use of door stops, wedges and other unapproved hold-open devices are prohibited. Where it is desired to keep the doors open, the fire chief may require the installation of approved smoke activated self-closing devices or, if appropriate, heat activated.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(r))
624:
(a) Any premises which the city fire department may be called upon to protect in case of fire or other emergency, and which is not readily accessible from public roads or to which access may be obstructed by parked vehicles, shall be provided with suitable access roads, fire lanes, gates, etc., so that all buildings on the premises are reasonably accessible to fire apparatus.
(b) Fire lanes shall be provided and adequately and clearly indicated for each commercial and public building by the owner or occupant of same when the need for a fire lane is determined to exist by the fire chief.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(s))
625:
(a) No person shall place or keep any fence, growth, trash or other material near any fire hydrant that would prevent such hydrant from being immediately discernible or in any other manner hinder the fire department from gaining immediate access to a fire hydrant.
(b) No authorized person shall use or operate any fire hydrant or any valve installed on any water system intended for use of the fire department for fire suppression or control purposes and which is accessible to any public highway, alley or private way open to or generally used by the public unless such person first secures proper authorization.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(t))
626:
No person, unless properly authorized, shall remove, unlock, destroy, tamper with or otherwise molest in any manner any lock, gate, door, barricade, chain, enclosure, sign, tag, notice or seal which has been lawfully installed by the fire chief or by his order or under his control.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-8(u))
628:
(a) Accumulations of combustible or flammable waste or refuse. Any person having control of any building, structure, facility, premises, or portion thereof, shall not allow or permit any combustible or flammable waste material or refuse to accumulate in any room, area or space in or on the building, structure, facility or premises in any manner so as to create a fire hazard or hazard to life or property in event of fire originating in or spreading to such an accumulation.
(b) Disposal of combustible or flammable waste or refuse.
(1) Any person having control of any building, structure, facility, premises, or portion thereof, shall be responsible for properly disposing of or properly storing combustible or flammable waste or refuse at the end of each working day. This disposal or proper storing shall occur before vacating the building, structure, facility, premises, or portion thereof, and whenever such may be necessary to prevent a fire hazard or other unsafe condition.
(2) All combustible or flammable waste, refuse, rubbish, oily rags or oily wastes at work spaces or areas during the day or work period shall be stored in metal, metal lined or approved rigid nonmetallic containers or receptacles. If the wastes, rags or refuse are subject to spontaneous heating or ignition, such shall be kept in metal or metal lined containers with tightfitting self-closing covers.
(3) Outdoor accumulations of combustible or flammable waste, refuse, litter and vegetation. Roofs, courts, yards and open spaces shall be kept free and clear of deposits or accumulations of waste paper, hay, grass, straw, weeds, old vehicle tires, combustible litter, rubbish, waste or refuse of any kind that creates a fire hazard as defined in this Code.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-9)
629:
(a) Smoking defined. For the purposes of this section and other provisions of this Code related to smoking, the term "smoking" shall be construed to mean and include the carrying of a lighted pipe, cigar, cigarette or any other device containing tobacco, or any other material for the purpose of inhaling or drawing the smoke or fumes from the glowing or smoldering material.
(b) Authority of fire chief. Where conditions are such as to make smoking a fire hazard in any building, structure or facility or on any premises, the fire chief is empowered to order the prohibiting of smoking and to order the posting of "NO SMOKING" signs in each room, space, area, building, structure, facility or premises in or on which smoking shall be prohibited. It is unlawful for any person to smoke where smoking is prohibited by order of the fire chief or his authorized representative during any emergency control operation.
(c) Safe smoking areas. The fire chief is empowered to approve locations where smoking is to be permitted, if he deems such to be appropriate, in any building, structure or facility or on any premises.
(d) Warning signs. The lettering, size, color and location of legally required "NO SMOKING" signs shall be subject to the approval of the fire chief. It is unlawful for any person to remove, mutilate or destroy any legally required "NO SMOKING" sign.
(e) Smoking restricted. It is unlawful for any person to smoke, throw or deposit any lighted or smoldering substance in any place where "NO SMOKING" signs are posted by order of the fire chief or where smoking would clearly constitute a hazard to life or property from fire.
(f) Outdoor smoking restrictions. It is unlawful for any person to light, ignite or otherwise set fire to or to smoke any tobacco or other substance or any cigarette, pipe, cigar or other device in or upon any brush or forest-covered land, or land covered with any flammable or combustible material, or upon any road or trail traversing any such land during any period of the year declared by the fire chief as hazardous due to dry conditions or atmospheric conditions, or at any time a hazard exists due to the spill or leakage of a hazardous material in the judgment of the fire chief or his representatives.
(g) Smoking in bed unlawful. It is unlawful for any person to smoke in bed in any hotel, motel or dormitory so as to cause a fire due to the careless use of smoking materials in any hotel, motel or dormitory.
(h) Disposal of smoking materials. Cigarette, cigars, pipe tobacco or other substances used in pipes, or matches shall not be discarded after use in any trash can, garbage can, waste or refuse container or in any trash or laundry chute. Such material shall be placed in proper ashtrays or other receptacles designated for the discard of used smoking materials and shall not be emptied into any trash chute or trash bin. The contents of ashtrays or receptacles designated for the proper discard of smoking material shall be emptied into covered metal containers or devices and such materials shall be wetted and checked to ensure they are completely extinguished of all glowing or smoldering prior to final disposal. The term "final disposal after being wetted and checked" may include emptying the materials into containers for the removal and disposal of other trash.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-10)
630:
(a) Every building and structure coming within the scope of this code shall be designed, constructed and maintained so as to provide adequate warning of a fire and so as to provide adequate and protected means of egress for occupants in the event of fire or other emergency or to provide reasonable areas of protective refuge in buildings where egress may not be practical under emergency conditions.
(b) In the case of existing buildings or structures, the fire chief may modify the provisions of the adopted life safety code pertaining to existing buildings or structures when there are practical difficulties in the way of carrying out the strict letter of the code; provided, however, the spirit of the code shall be observed, public safety reasonably protected, and substantial justice done. The particulars of such modification when granted or allowed, and the decision of the fire chief thereon shall be entered upon the records of the fire department.
(c) In every building or structure where seats, tables, merchandise, equipment, numbers of people or similar impediments to egress are present, required aisles, corridors, passages and other means of egress shall be maintained free of impediments to emergency egress.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-11(a)—(c))
631:
(a) In any building or portion of a building or structure used as a place of assembly, as defined by the life safety code, or in other buildings or structures or portions thereof as required by the building code, the number of occupants thereof shall not be permitted to exceed the allowed or posted capacity established by the fire chief or the building official.
(b) For purposes of this section, it shall be prima facie evidence of an overcrowding condition when either there are more people in the building or portion thereof than has been allowed or posted, or when, in the judgment of the fire chief or his representative, a threat to the safety of life exists due to the number of persons sitting or standing so as to obstruct or impede the use of aisles, passages, corridors or exits.
(c) It is the responsibility of the owner, manager or person in charge of a building, structure, or portion thereof, to prevent an overcrowding condition to exist and to take prompt action to remedy an overcrowding condition when so advised or ordered by the fire chief or his representative. It is unlawful for the owner, manager or person thereof, to knowingly permit an overcrowding condition to exist.
(Code 1989, § 3-2-11(d))

669:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abate means to repair, replace, remove, destroy or otherwise remedy the condition in question by such means and in such a manner and to such an extent as the enforcement officer, in his judgment, determines is necessary in the interest of the general health, safety and welfare of the community.
Blighted property means any property on which there exists any one or more of the following conditions or activities:
(1) A building or structure that is not occupied, inhabited, used, or secured. For purposes of this article, a building or structure is unsecured when it is unlocked or the public can gain entry without the consent of the owner.
(2) Any partially constructed, reconstructed or demolished building or structure upon which work is abandoned. Work is deemed abandoned when there is no valid and current building or demolition permit or when there has not been any substantial work on the project for six months.
(3) Property which is in an unsecured state so as to potentially constitute an attraction to children, a harbor for vagrants, criminals, or other unauthorized persons, or so as to enable persons to resort thereto for the purpose of committing a nuisance or unlawful act.
(4) Any building or other structure which by reason of rot, weakened joints, walls, floors, underpinning, roof, ceilings, or insecure foundation, or other cause has become dilapidated or deteriorated.
(5) Any building or other structure with exterior walls or roof coverings that have become so deteriorated as to not provide adequate weather protection and be likely to, or have resulted in, termite infestation or dry rot.
(6) Buildings or structures including, but not limited to, walls, windows, fences, signs, substantially defaced to the extent that the disrepair visually impacts on neighboring property or presents a risk to public safety. For purposes of this article the term "defaced" includes, but is not limited to, writings, inscriptions, figures, scratches, or other markings commonly referred to as "graffiti" and peeling, flaking, blistering, or otherwise deteriorated paint.
(7) Property which is not kept clean and sanitary and free from all accumulations of offensive matter or odor including, but not limited to, overgrown or dead or decayed trees weeds or other vegetation, rank growth, dead organic matter, rubbish, junk, garbage, animal intestinal waste and urine, and toxic or otherwise hazardous liquids and substances and materials.
(8) Property which constitutes a fire hazard or a condition considered dangerous to the public health, safety, and general welfare.
(9) Property which is likely to or does harbor rats or other vermin, feral pets, or other non-domesticated animal nuisances.
(10) Property which substantially detracts from the aesthetic and economic values of neighboring properties including, but not limited to, personal property and wares and foodstuffs, premises garbage and refuse receptacles, and commercial and industrial business activities which are inadequately buffered from any street, sidewalk, or other publicly trafficked area or such buffering which is inadequately maintained.
(11) Landscaping which is inadequately maintained or which is not installed as required by city codes or any permit issued in accordance with such codes.
(12) Matter including, but not limited to, smoke, odors, dust, dirt, debris, fumes, and sprays which are permitted to be transported by wind or otherwise upon any street, course, alley, sidewalk, yard, park, or other public or private property and which are determined to be a violation of federal, state, regional, or local air quality regulations.
(13) Property including, but not limited to, building facade, window, doorway, driveway, walkway, fence, wall, landscaped planter or area, sidewalk, curb and gutter, and edge of street pavement on which dirt, litter, vegetation, garbage, refuse, debris, flyers, or circulars have accumulated.
(14) Property on which a swimming pool, pond, stream, or other body of water which is abandoned, unattended, unfiltered, or not otherwise maintained, resulting in the water becoming polluted. The term "polluted water" is defined for the purpose of this article, as water which contains bacterial growth, remains of garbage, refuse, debris, papers and any other foreign matter or material which constitutes an unhealthy or unsafe condition.
(15) Parking lots, driveways, paths, and other areas used or intended to be used for commercial and industrial business activities including, but not limited to, selling, manufacturing, processing, packaging, fabricating, treating, dismantling, processing, transferring, handling, transporting, storing, compounding, or assembling which are inadequately maintained and pose a risk of harm to public health or safety including, but not limited to, unpaved surfaces which generate fugitive dust and paved surfaces with cracks, potholes, or other breaks.
(16) Property which is not securely fenced or adequately lighted to prevent illegal access and activity related to the dumping of garbage, waste, debris and litter.
(17) Property having a topography, geology, or configuration which, as a result of grading operations, erosion control, sedimentation control work, or other improvements to the property, causes erosion, subsidence, unstable soil conditions, or surface or subsurface drainage problems as to harm or pose a risk of harm to adjacent properties.
(18) Property whereon any condition or object obscures the visibility of public street intersections to the public so as to constitute a hazard, including, but not limited to, landscaping, fencing, signs, posts, or equipment.
(19) Conditions which, due to their accessibility to the public, pose a hazard including, but not limited to, unused and broken equipment, abandoned wells, shafts, or basements, hazardous or unprotected pools, ponds, or excavations, structurally unsound fences or structures, machinery which is inadequately secured or protected, lumber, trash, fences or debris that may pose a hazard to the public, storage of chemicals, gas, oil, or toxic or flammable liquids.
Junk means and includes the storage of all old appliances, equipment or parts thereof, all old iron or other scrap metal, all inoperable vehicles or parts thereof, including tires, all vehicle hulks, cardboard, all lumber, old wood and mattresses, which items are not being used for their intended purpose. The term "junk" does not include orderly stacked firewood.
Litter means and includes all waste material, including, but not limited to, disposable packages or containers thrown or deposited on public or private property, including the depositing of handbills on public property or cars, but not including the waste of the primary process of mining, logging, sawmilling, farming or manufacturing.
Premises means any building, lot, parcel, real estate, land or portion of land, whether improved or unimproved, including adjacent sidewalks and parking strips.
Refuse means vegetable offal, animal offal, discarded food, cans, bottles, waste paper, large tree limbs and all other waste substances from private and public establishments and from residences. The term "refuse" does not include small amounts of weeds, twigs, grass or other material resulting from the normal tending of lawns and gardens.
Responsible person means any agent, lessee, owner or other person occupying or having charge or control of any premises.
Rubbish means and includes combustible and noncombustible waste materials, except garbage; the residue from the burning of wood, coal, coke, and other combustible material; paper, rags, cartons, boxes, wood, excelsior, rubber, leather, tree branches, yard trimmings, hay, straw, tin cans, metal, mineral matter, glass, crockery, and dust. The term "rubbish" shall also include animal feed and the products of and residue from animal quarters.
Weed, vegetable growth and horticultural growth means and includes, but is not limited to, trees, plants, shrubs, bushes, flowers, garden vegetables and grasses and further includes all growths of every kind and character, whether domestic or wild, causing the obstruction or interference or detriment prohibited by this article.
(Code 1989, § 9-2-2; Ord. of 4-11-2005, § II(9-2-2); Ord. of 9-8-2008, § II(9-2-2))
